newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent slightly softer ahead of August expiry.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent slightly softer ahead of August expiry.

text.p: IPE Brent futures softened on Wednesday ahead of the August contract expiry after building on Tuesday in expectation of bullish industry stock data from the United States, brokers said.

Reports that Iraq would be unable to carry more than five percent of its $1 billion quarterly limit for oil sales into the second 90 day period of the oil-for-food deal with the U.N. were having little market effect.
"There are people saying this was built in to the market, others saying it was not built in," said one broker.
"But at the end of the day I think people were expecting lower numbers yesterday and then they got caught short when it went up. The news itself was by and large not very relevant."

August Brent, which expires on Wednesday, stood four cents a barrel down at 1149 GMT at $18.35. September Brent was two cents down at the same price while August gas oil was $1.25 a tonne up at $164.00.
"It is mostly just a bit of fun and games because of the expiry today," one dealer at the IPE said.
The American Petroleum Institute (API) said in a weekly report released overnight that U.S. crude stocks had fallen by about 5.4 million barrels.
Gasoline inventories were some 3.5 million million barrels down on the week.
This led to a sharp, late rally on futures on Tuesday. "Speculation or otherwise, there seemed to be a clear expectation of the gasoline figure in late trade," brokers GNI said in a daily report.

Iraq, having delayed the restart of oil exports for two months, will have to sell oil at a much higher rate in August than was previously thought in order to sell a billion dollars' worth of oil by the 90 day deadline.
The U.N. resolution allowing the oil sales came into effect on June 8.
One dealer said on Wednesday he thought this news had had only a limited effect on prices.
